facts.statement: The genus Hauffiosaurus was first named by Frank Robin O'Keefe in 2001, with Hauffiosaurus zanoni designated as the type species.
facts.quote: It was first named by Frank Robin O'Keefe in 2001 and the type species is Hauffiosaurus zanoni.

facts.statement: Two additional species, H. longirostris and H. tomistomimus, were assigned to the genus Hauffiosaurus in 2011.
facts.quote: In 2011, two additional species were assigned to this genus: H. longirostris and H. tomistomimus.

facts.statement: Hauffiosaurus lived during the Early Jurassic (early Toarcian stage) and is known from fossil sites in Holzmaden, Germany, and Yorkshire, United Kingdom.
facts.quote: Hauffiosaurus is an extinct genus of Early Jurassic (early Toarcian stage) pliosaurid plesiosaur known from Holzmaden of Germany and from Yorkshire of the United Kingdom.

facts.statement: Hauffiosaurus zanoni was a medium-sized plesiosaur measuring approximately 3.4 meters in length.
facts.quote: Hauffiosaurus zanoni is a plesiosaur of medium size, measuring 3.4 m.

facts.statement: The skull of Hauffiosaurus zanoni measures about 430 mm along the midline.
facts.quote: The skull measures about 430 mm along the midline.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Hauffiosaurus tomistomimus measures 4.83 meters in length.
facts.quote: The holotype of H. tomistomimus measures 4.83 m long.

facts.statement: The individual belonging to the holotype of Hauffiosaurus longirostris is estimated to have measured approximately 4.83 meters in total body length.
facts.quote: The individual to which this specimen belongs is estimated to have measured approximately 4.83 m in total body length.

facts.statement: The teeth of Hauffiosaurus were slender, elongated, and possessed fine longitudinal ridges.
facts.quote: The teeth are slender and elongated and possess fine longitudinal ridges.

facts.statement: The combination of slender, ridged teeth and a long rostrum in Hauffiosaurus was effective for piercing soft prey.
facts.quote: This sort of tooth, coupled with the long rostrum seen in this genus is effective in piercing soft prey.

facts.statement: Smith & Dyke (2008) were the first to identify Hauffiosaurus as a basal pliosauroid.
facts.quote: Smith & Dyke, 2008 were the first who found Hauffiosaurus to be basal pliosauroid.

facts.statement: Hauffiosaurus lived from 184.2 to 174.7 million years ago during the Toarcian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Toarcian (184.2 to 174.7 million years ago)

rejected.quote: Few Early Jurassic plesiosaurians have the sort of long, thin snout present in Hauffiosaurus, a shape usually considered to indicate a diet of fish (ichthyophagy).
